I’m 67 this year, and it’s just me and my wife working the land. My son is off in Shijiazhuang doing construction, so we can’t count on his help except maybe at wheat harvest. After 40 years I know every corner of these 16 mu, and I don’t take risks anymore. The wheat-maize double crop is my safety net — if one fails, the other usually gets us through. I plant 15 mu to that rotation. The other 1.1 mu is stevia. I started that about six years back when the buyer came to the village promising good prices. It pays better than grain per mu, but the picking is hard on my back, so I won’t expand it. At my age, stable is better than greedy.

The wheat went in last October like always — I used improved seed from the co-op, the same kind my neighbor Lao Zhang buys. I rotary-tilled before planting because the soil gets hard over summer. Now it’s greening up, so I’ll topdress with urea and irrigate four times total this year: green-up, jointing, heading, and grain filling. That’s what everyone in the village does, and I’ve got the well. For maize, the window between wheat harvest and planting is only about five days, so I use no-tillage planting with a hybrid variety — saves time, saves diesel, and the crop still gets 500 jin or more per mu. I fertilize maize lighter than wheat because it’s a shorter season. For the stevia, since it’s perennial I just do light rotary weeding between rows. It needs more frequent watering to keep the leaves tender, and I spray more often because those leaf miners love it.

Here is my plan for the year:
